transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Horizon CISO), Raj Patel (Horizon Head of Cloud), Sophie Li (Horizon Compliance)

Summary:
High-level posture review of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts, access to the Trust Center, controls mapping for Horizon's regulatory needs (HIPAA subset), and technical clarifications around audit logs, encryption/KMS, KMS/HSM, RBAC/SSO (SAML), data residency (EU), and private/VPC deployment patterns. Action items captured at end.

Topics:
- Trust Center access and artifact sharing (SOC 2, ISO cert)
- Controls mapping (Redwood controls -> Horizon control ids)
- Audit logs: retention, access, export to SIEM
- Encryption: KMS integration, HSM options, key ownership
- Identity and access: SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC roles
- Data residency and private deployment (VPC/on-prem)
- Operational aspects: SLA, dedicated pools, fallback and traceability

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE, and with me is Diego, our security solutions engineer.
[00:08] Raj Patel: Hey, Raj here, thanks. We have Lena and Sophie on for the compliance side.
[00:12] Lena Park: Hi all.
[00:15] Diego Ruiz: Great, quick agenda 


we want to walk through the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, show how you can access the Trust Center, and then dig into audit logs, KMS, and SSO details. Is that okay?
[00:25] Sophie Li: Yep, that's perfect. Our main ask today is to confirm whether your SOC 2 covers the kind of data flows we have and how controls map to our HIPAA requirements.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Totally. Also note: we'll share the Trust Center link after the call. Link will include the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and the ISO 27001 certificate. The link is something like https://trust.redwood.ai 


we'll send exact.
[00:45] Raj Patel: One quick qualifier, we run primarily in AWS and some Azure for DR, and we need EU data residency for EEA tenants. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning and VPC options?
[00:55] Diego Ruiz: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning on hosted, and for stricter isolation we have Redwood Private 

VPC or on-prem options. Small note, I may say 'Redwood Dedicaed' sometimes, sorry, meant Dedicated. For VPC, we provide a private control plane and customer-managed networking so traffic never leaves your VPC.
[01:20] Lena Park: Good. On the SOC 2 itself, does it include logging controls for admin actions and access to keys? We need auditability of who accessed what and when.
[01:30] Diego Ruiz: The SOC 2 report covers access controls and change management for the control plane. We also provide audit logs exports 

you can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or push to S3 with lifecycle policies. Logs include admin console actions, API calls, and model inference request metadata (note: inference payloads are redacted in standard logs).
[01:55] Sophie Li: Retention policies? We need at least 1 year of immutable logs for our internal audit.
[02:02] Maya Chen: Default retention is 90 days in the console, but for enterprise customers we offer configurable retention and longer-term archival to your S3 or object store 

that supports 1+ years. We can also provide WORM style policies if needed.
[02:20] Raj Patel: About KMS, we have a customer-managed key requirement. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or an HSM?
[02:27] Diego Ruiz: Yes. We support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) with AWS KMS integration and can do envelope encryption. For HSM-grade keys, we can integrate with cloud HSM providers; for private deployments you can manage keys on-prem or via an HSM appliance. There may be an extra compliance review for HSM workflows.
[02:48] Lena Park: Who holds the keys by default?
[02:50] Diego Ruiz: By default Redwood manages service keys, but enterprise contracts can include BYOK so Horizon holds the customer master key 

Redwood stores only encrypted data and can't decrypt without your key.
[03:03] Sophie Li: Good. What about separation of duties and RBAC? We need fine-grained roles, and SSO integration with SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[03:12] Maya Chen: We have RBAC baked in 

admin, operator, auditor, and custom roles. SAML SSO is supported along with SCIM for user provisioning. Diego, do you want to add on policy-level audit?
[03:24] Diego Ruiz: Sure. All role changes and SSO events are recorded in audit logs. There is also token-level tracing for API keys. For audit we can produce CSV exports for the time period you request. Occasionally speech-to-text transcribes 'tokens' as 'tockens' in our old notes, but the data is fine.
[03:44] Raj Patel: On data residency, if we pin to eu-west-1, does any metadata or control-plane traffic route through US?
[03:50] Diego Ruiz: For hosted EU customers we provide regional control planes to minimize cross-border metadata flow. Some global services (billing, billing-alerts) may still touch other regions, but we can document the exact flows. For strict residency we recommend Redwood Private inside your VPC or on-prem to ensure no outbound control plane egress.
[04:12] Lena Park: Let's talk controls mapping. We need a spreadsheet mapping Redwood controls to our HIPAA and internal SOC requirements 

is that something you provide?
[04:20] Maya Chen: Yes, Diego will provide a controls mapping template. We'll pre-fill high-level mappings from our SOC 2 report to common frameworks (SOC2->ISO->HIPAA) and then work with you to map specifics. We'll redact any sensitive operational details before sharing.
[04:35] Diego Ruiz: I'll attach an initial mapping and notes. Heads-up: some low-level infra controls reference our runtime optimizations 

e.g., KV cache isolation, continuous batching 

which are implementation details, we'll summarize at control level not low-level kernel names.
[04:55] Sophie Li: For the audit committee we also need a copy of your ISO 27001 scope and the certificate.
[05:00] Maya Chen: We'll include the ISO 27001 certificate in the Trust Center link. It's a public cert that shows scope including the hosted and dedicated offerings.
[05:10] Raj Patel: Regarding RPO/RTO and SLAs, are those in the dedicated offering?
[05:15] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, configurable autoscaling, and reserved GPU pools. For mission-critical workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private, depending on your isolation needs.
[05:30] Raj Patel: Can we run a scoping POC where we validate latency, token cost, and correctness on a subset of patient data in a redacted form?
[05:40] Maya Chen: Absolutely 

common pattern: POC in Dedicated with a small reserved capacity, run benchmarks, and map costs. We'll provide sample prompts and evaluation harness. Diego, we'll need to support secure ingestion 

plugin?
[05:53] Diego Ruiz: Yep, we have secure ingestion pipelines that can push directly into a customer S3 or into a VPC endpoint. For patient data we strongly recommend sending hashed or tokenized data during POC until contracts are finalized.
[06:08] Sophie Li: On the contractual side, we also need SOC 2 type II AICPA attestation and ability to do penetration testing or at least see your testing schedule.
[06:18] Diego Ruiz: The SOC 2 attestation is in the Trust Center. For pen test, we have a disclosure policy 

customers can run tests after coordination; for private deployments you can run internal tests. We'll share the pentest program summary.
[06:32] Lena Park: A couple of nitty gritty items: who can access raw inference logs internally at Redwood? We need to limit personnel.
[06:40] Diego Ruiz: Access is role-based and limited to a small ops team under NDA, with just-in-time escalation and session recording. Engineering access to production datasets is rare and monitored. Those specifics are in the SOC 2 supplemental notes.
[06:55] Raj Patel: For KMS, is key rotation automatic? And do you offer HSM-backed rotation policies?
[07:02] Diego Ruiz: With BYOK via AWS KMS you can control rotation. Redwood supports automatic rotation policies if you want us to manage the key lifecycle, but for HSM-backed keys rotation is managed by the HSM/service. We'll document the exact flow.
[07:18] Sophie Li: Can we get a vendor risk assessment template pre-filled?
[07:22] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide a vendor risk assessment and a pre-filled security questionnaire (common frameworks). We'll also include contact for escalation and our SOC 2 auditor name.
[07:34] Lena Park: One more: do you provide access to raw audit logs via API for ingestion into our SIEM, or is it only S3/Push?
[07:43] Diego Ruiz: You can pull logs via API or set up push to S3/Kafka 

for real-time SIEM ingestion we recommend push to your log collector in the same region to avoid cross-region transfer.
[07:58] Raj Patel: About encryption in transit: do you support mTLS between our services and Redwood endpoints?
[08:05] Diego Ruiz: TLS is standard; for mutual TLS we can add mTLS for private deployments or Dedicated with dedicated networking. For hosted customers we provide strong TLS and client cert options under enterprise agreements.
[08:20] Sophie Li: Any notes about data deletion and residuals 

can you confirm deletion upon contract end?
[08:26] Maya Chen: We have data deletion policies tied to contracts. For private deployments you control data retention entirely. For hosted we follow deletion requests and can provide certification of deletion for covered data after a retention period.
[08:40] Lena Park: Great. Can we do a quick recap of next deliverables?
[08:45] Maya Chen: Sure 

action items: I'll send Trust Center link with SOC2 and ISO artifacts; Diego will send controls mapping template and a pentest program summary; Raj will share the list of regulatory controls to be mapped and target pilot date. We'll schedule the on-prem demo.
[09:00] Sophie Li: Timeline 

Horizon is aiming for an internal audit in late Q2, so we'd like the mapping and POC to run in April/May.
[09:10] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll prioritize Diego's deliverables.
[09:15] (background noise)
[09:20] Raj Patel: Quick follow-up 

for the POC, do you support sample rate-limiting and throttling to model variants to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs?
[09:28] Diego Ruiz: Yes, Redwood routing policies let you route by latency vs cost 

you can pin certain requests to cheaper quantized variants or to full-precision in Dedicated. We also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model if capacity spikes.
[09:45] Lena Park: On the controls mapping, we need explicit references to evidence artifacts 

can you attach which logs or reports prove each control?
[09:53] Diego Ruiz: We'll annotate the mapping with evidence pointers: e.g., control SOC2-A3 -> audit log export (s3://...), pentest report section 4.2, ISO control A.9 etc. We'll avoid including sensitive runtime details in the public mapping.
[10:10] Maya Chen: OK, we'll wrap. Thanks everyone for time. We'll send materials by Friday.
[10:18] Sophie Li: Thanks, very helpful.
[10:20] Lena Park: Thanks.
[10:22] (call ends)

References and links mentioned (to be sent):

- Timeline: Horizon targeting late Q2 internal audit; aim to run mapping and POC in April/May.
